item.title: Public Bioethics: Can Ordinary People Navigate Extraordinary Questions? — Thu Sep 10, 5:00 PM — None
item.description:
In an era of declining trust in medicine, science, and healthcare institutions, there is good reason to consider how to foster a more public conversation about the aims, goals, and ethics of medicine. Bioethics is not something that belongs only to academics, physicians, and policymakers but to everyone affected by healthcare decisions-which is to say, everyone. Dr. Stahl explores how public bioethics can help ordinary people navigate extraordinary moral questions by making ethical reflection accessible, inclusive, and grounded in real human lives.
Devan Stahl, PhD, MDiv, is an Associate Professor of Bioethics and Religion at Baylor University and Adjunct Associate Professor in the Department of Education, Innovation, and Technology at the Baylor College of Medicine. Dr. Stahl serves as the Associate Director of the Baylor Center for Ethics and volunteers as a clinical ethics consultant for Baylor Scott & White Hillcrest Hospital. She is also the cohost of the popular podcast Bioethic

item.description:

"Her Fight, His Name: The Story of Gwen Carr and Eric Garner" (Brad Bailey, 2024, 30m)
A community discussion with director Brad Bailey and Mrs. Gwen Carr, and led by Natalie Bullock-Brown, will follow the screening.
The short documentary centers on Gwen Carr's enduring fight for justice following the 2014 death of her son, Eric Garner, after being pinned to the ground in a chokehold by a police officer in Staten Island. The New York City medical examiner stated the cause of death as a homicide. Garner's final words, "I can't breathe," became a rallying cry in protests against police violence and systemic racism across the United States. Filmed over several years, the documentary places Carr's voice at its core, tracing her transformation from grieving mother to nationally recognized advocate for accountability and human rights.

item.title: Closing Screening of “Til Íslands” — Thu Sep 10, 7:00 PM — Center for Documentary Studies
item.description:
Join us for the closing screening of "Til Íslands," artist and Duke alum Emma Geiger's experimental documentary short film, and a last chance to visit her exhibition of the same name.
Schedule
• 7 p.m. - Experience "Til Íslands" one final time in the CDS Kreps Gallery • 8 p.m. - Attend a screening of "Til Íslands" in the CDS auditorium followed by a Q&A session moderated by Alexa Dilworth
About the Screening
Returning to the Icelandic landscape left behind by her great-great-grandparents in 1888, "Til Íslands" (meaning "To Iceland" in Icelandic) documents the delicate experience of the filmmaker's reconnection with a land and people in the midst of dramatic environmental change. Shot on 8mm and 16mm film, along with cameraless imagery created by placing plants, seaweed, and wool directly on the film, this experimental documentary short invites viewers into a conversation between past and present, in which the plants, animals, water, and people of the landscape all take part.

item.description:
"The Samurai and the Prisoner" ["Kokurojo"] (Kiyoshi Kurosawa, 2026, 147 min, Japan, Japanese with English subtitles, DCP)
An Official Selection of the 2026 Cannes Film Festival, Kurosawa Kiyoshi's enthralling adaptation of Yonezawa Honobu's prize-winning novel is his first foray into jidaigeki, blending samurai cinema with the murder mystery genre. Kurosawa shows his mastery of the cinematic craft by navigating the novel's dense narrative with a confident hand, slowly pulling in the audience with an absorbing moral contemplation on the nature of war, and a variation on a familiar genre that is both classical and radical.
The story follows Lord Murashige Araki (Motoki), who, after rising up against the tyrannical warlord Nobunaga Oda, finds himself besieged within his own Arioka Castle. item.description:

This presentation includes two exemplar studies within PAC.

item.title: Pressing Prompts Workshop (Online) — Fri Sep 11, 12:00 PM — Virtual
item.description:
Incubated at Duke, Pressing Prompts (pressingprompts.org) is an open education resource for instructors across all disciplines who are seeking ways to integrate AI ethics into their classrooms. Unlike a static set of "best practices," Pressing Prompts is grounded in principles of critical pedagogy and educational experimentation, encouraging instructors and students to examine how AI raises crucial questions about our academic responsibilities, knowledge, labor, judgment, and learning.
In this workshop, we will offer: a brief overview of Pressing Prompts within the larger context of AI, ethics, and education; scaffolded opportunities to experiment with Pressing Prompts to consider how it might fit into one of your classroom conversations, assignments, or larger course units; and a facilitated conversation for sharing ideas between faculty peers.
Source: Duke University

item.title: Hawkwatch on the Blue Ridge Parkway (Candler) — Fri Sep 18, 10:00 AM
item.description:
Join NCWF ReWild AVL for a morning of hawk watching with Mark Waligora, owner of Wild Birds Unlimited South Asheville, and Vicky Burke, Hawkwatch Coordinator. Hawk migration typically peaks in the Asheville area around September 19–25, and around 10:00 a.m. the mountain thermals begin to build, creating ideal conditions for migrating raptors to take flight. Vicky will share her expertise about this important hawkwatch location and help us spot and identify migrating raptors. On a good morning, you may see up to 14 species of hawks and other raptors as they soar overhead! We’ll meet at the Mills River Overlook – Mile Marker 404.5 on the Blue Ridge Parkway approximately three miles before the Pisgah Inn when traveling from Asheville. Space is limited and registration is required, so be sure to reserve your spot! REGISTER HERE
Source: NC Wildlife Federation

item.title: Flat Creek Bioblitz! (Montreat) — Fri Sep 18, 1:30 PM
item.description:
Join NCWF Swannanoa Valley Wild for a Bioblitz along Flat Creek in Montreat. We’ll work together to identify plants, amphibians, reptiles, mammals, birds, and all things WILD. Bioblitzes are a great way to connect to the environment while generating useful data for science and conservation. This effort is a part of the “Flat Creek 2040” project working to foster awareness, understanding, and engagement with Flat Creek and its watershed on the part of researchers, community members, officials, and educators. item.description: Join NCWF South Wake Conservationists Chapter at Inwood Wildlife Garden for a hands-on volunteer day as we build our first-ever hibernaculum! A hibernaculum is a protective shelter or refuge that wildlife uses to survive the winter dormancy period. Typically constructed using natural materials such as rocks, logs, branches, and stones, these structures create protected spaces for reptiles, amphibians, insects, and small mammals during the colder months. We’ll have the materials needed for construction on hand. Not into building a hibernaculum? We have plenty to do! There are lots of other ways to lend a hand at Inwood Wildlife Garden, including weeding the pollinator garden, mulching garden paths, planting aquatic plants around the wildlife pond, and helping with general garden maintenance. item.title: America 250! Revolutionary War Patriots Marker Dedication — Thu Oct 1, 10:30 AM — Moore County Courthouse
item.description:
The Alfred Moore Chapter, National Society Daughters of the American Revolution (NSDAR), invites the community to attend the dedication and unveiling of an America 250! Revolutionary War Patriots Marker.
The marker will be placed on the courthouse grounds adjacent to the Charters of Freedom and will serve as a permanent tribute to the men and women whose courage, sacrifice, and service helped secure American independence.
The dedication is part of the National Society Daughters of the American Revolution’s nationwide commemoration of the 250th anniversary of the United States. Through its America 250! initiatives, DAR is honoring the Patriots of the American Revolution and encouraging communities to reflect upon the people, events, and ideals that shaped the founding of our nation.
